question: A company director is attempting to submit claims for an Overseas Market Preparation (OMP) Grant with reference ID 240799EZ. The director discovered that the claims submission closing date in the Business Grants Portal (BGP) is set to 30 December 2025 instead of 31 December 2025, which is the actual last day of the month, and the portal has closed before the director could submit the claims.
expected_outcome: The director receives confirmation that Enterprise Singapore has received the change request to reactivate the grant in the BGP Portal and understands that the request is under review with a response to come.
enquiry_text: Ref ID: 240799EZ Claims submission Alex Neo  [EMAIL]  Wed 31/12/2025, 20:19 ENTERPRISESG enquiries-reply (ENTERPRISESG)  Dear Mark,  I'm trying to submit the claims for the above mentioned OMP Grant but realise that the closing date is 30/12/25 instead of 31/12/25 which is the actual last day of the month. Pls help to reactivate the grant in BGP Portal so that I can process and submit the claims. Thank you and Happy New Year.  Regards Alex Neo Director
answer_text:
Enterprise Singapore acknowledged receipt of the change request submission on 2 January 2026 at 10:18 AM.
The change request for Grant reference ID 240799EZ is currently under review by the Enterprise Singapore team.
Enterprise Singapore will be in touch regarding the review outcome as soon as possible.

claims.claim: Enterprise Singapore acknowledged receipt of the change request submission on 2 January 2026 at 10:18 AM.
claims.source: Enterprise Singapore processes change requests submitted through the BGP portal within 5 to 10 working days. An automated acknowledgement email is sent to the primary contact upon successful submission, confirming receipt of the request and the reference ID assigned.

claims.claim: The change request for Grant reference ID 240799EZ is currently under review by the Enterprise Singapore team.
claims.source: Change requests for active grants are reviewed by an assigned Enterprise Singapore officer. The review period may vary depending on the nature of the change — extensions to Claim Due Dates typically take 3 to 7 working days. Status updates are sent via email to the applicant's registered address.

claims.claim: Enterprise Singapore will be in touch regarding the review outcome as soon as possible.

sources.title: ESG Claims Processing Guidelines v2.4
sources.excerpt: Claims must be submitted within the grant approval period. If the portal displays an incorrect closing date, the applicant should contact the administering agency immediately with their grant reference number to request a date correction or portal reactivation. The agency will review the request within 3 working days.

sources.title: Market Readiness Assistance Grant — Enterprise Singapore

answer_text: Application status updates for SSG Tech Grant submissions are managed by the SSG helpdesk. Please contact them directly with your application reference number and they will be able to assist you.

claims.claim: Application status updates for SSG Tech Grant submissions are managed by the SSG helpdesk. Please contact them directly with your application reference number and they will be able to assist you.
claims.source: SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) manages all application status communications for SSG-administered grants, including the SSG Tech Grant. Enquiries about application status should be directed to SSG directly as Enterprise Singapore does not have visibility into SSG's internal processing systems.

claims.source: The SSG Tech Grant supports companies in adopting technology solutions to improve productivity. It is administered end-to-end by SkillsFuture Singapore. Companies may check application status via the SkillsFuture for Business portal or contact the SSG hotline at 6785 5785.

claims.source: SSG can be reached at: Hotline 6785 5785 (Mon–Fri, 8:30am–5:30pm), Email business@ssg.gov.sg, or in person at 1 Marina Boulevard, #18-01 One Marina Boulevard, Singapore 018989.

question: A company has submitted retrospective applications for speed limiters and is waiting for a final response from the Land Transport Authority (LTA). The case has been kept open while awaiting LTA's decision on all the retrospective applications.
expected_outcome: The user understands the current status of their retrospective speed limiter applications with the Land Transport Authority.
enquiry_text: Keeping the case open while pending TP's final response regarding all retro applications for Speed Limiters
answer_text: The Land Transport Authority is reviewing the retrospective speed limiter applications

claims.claim: The Land Transport Authority is reviewing the retrospective speed limiter applications
claims.source: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) reviews retrospective applications for speed limiter compliance on a case-by-case basis. Processing timelines are subject to volume and the completeness of submitted documentation. LTA will contact the applicant via registered email once a decision has been made.

sources.title: LTA — Speed Limiter Retrofit Programme FAQ
sources.excerpt: Retrospective applications for speed limiters submitted before the programme deadline are subject to review by LTA. Applicants will be notified of the outcome by post or email. Processing times may vary depending on the volume of applications received.

question: A company submitted a Change Request on 25 December 2025 to extend their Claim Due Date from 29 December 2025 because they have not completed the audit for their Enterprise Development Grant claim. The caller is enquiring about the status of this Change Request with reference number 241154BK-CR01.
expected_outcome: The caller understands that the Change Request requires time to process and knows the proper claim submission procedure, including the requirement to select an auditor from Enterprise Singapore's Pre-Qualified Panel and wait for Change Request approval before submitting the claim.
enquiry_text: 241154BK-CR01    Agency:Enterprise Singapore           Caller enquiring on the above Change Request submitted on   25 Dec 2025, to extend the Claim Due Date because they have not completed the Audit.Initial Claim Due Date: 29 Dec 2025        Caller enquiring on the status of the above Change Request.
answer_text:
The Change Request will require some time to process.
The company should have submitted the claim before the Claim Due Date.
During final claim submission in BGP, the company must select an auditor from Enterprise Singapore's Pre-Qualified Panel to verify the claims.
An Enterprise Singapore officer will verify that the project deliverables have been met.
The Enterprise Singapore officer may contact the company for further information if required.
A site visit or presentation meeting may be arranged for the purpose of verifying project deliverables.
The company may be asked to revise the Project Report if the information is incomplete.
The auditor that the company has appointed will verify the claim documents and issue an Audit Report upon completion of the verification.
The company should wait for the approval of the Change Request before submitting the claim.

claims.claim: The Change Request will require some time to process.
claims.source: Change requests submitted through the BGP portal require manual review by an Enterprise Singapore officer. Standard processing time is 5 to 10 working days from the date of submission. Complex requests involving scope changes or budget revisions may take longer.

claims.claim: The company should have submitted the claim before the Claim Due Date.
claims.source: Under BGP grant conditions, all claims must be submitted on or before the Claim Due Date stated in the Letter of Offer. Retrospective change requests to extend the Claim Due Date are assessed at Enterprise Singapore's discretion and are not guaranteed to be approved.

claims.claim: During final claim submission in BGP, the company must select an auditor from Enterprise Singapore's Pre-Qualified Panel to verify the claims.
claims.source: During final claim submission in BGP, companies must select a pre-approved audit firm to verify claim documents. The auditor selection screen appears in Step 3 of the claim submission flow. Companies should ensure their appointed auditor is pre-registered in the BGP system before submission.

claims.claim: An Enterprise Singapore officer will verify that the project deliverables have been met.
claims.source: Enterprise Singapore officers conduct a deliverables verification review as part of the final claim assessment. This involves checking that all project deliverables stated in the approved project scope have been completed and are supported by adequate documentation.

claims.claim: The Enterprise Singapore officer may contact the company for further information if required.
A site visit or presentation meeting may be arranged for the purpose of verifying project deliverables.
claims.source: Site visits or presentation meetings may be arranged at the officer's discretion, particularly for projects with a high grant quantum or complex deliverables. The officer will contact the company at least 5 working days in advance to schedule the visit.

claims.claim: The company may be asked to revise the Project Report if the information is incomplete.
claims.source: If the Project Report does not adequately describe the outcomes achieved, the assigned officer will issue a revision request via the BGP portal. Companies are typically given 5 working days to resubmit the revised report.

claims.claim: The auditor that the company has appointed will verify the claim documents and issue an Audit Report upon completion of the verification.
claims.source: The appointed auditor's role is to verify the accuracy of the claim documents, including receipts, invoices, and proof of payment. Auditors must be selected from the approved panel listed in the BGP portal and must be independent of the company.

claims.claim: The company should wait for the approval of the Change Request before submitting the claim.

sources.title: BGP — How to submit a Change Request
EDG Claim Submission Guide — Auditor Requirements
sources.excerpt: All EDG claims above $30,000 must be verified by an auditor from Enterprise Singapore's Pre-Qualified Panel. The company is responsible for appointing the auditor before final claim submission. The auditor will issue an Audit Report which must be uploaded in BGP as part of the claim package.

question: A caller is experiencing a technical issue with the Business Growth Programme (BGP) 2.0 Grant Reimbursement Tracker (GRT) system where they are unable to submit their claim because clicking the next button does not proceed. They have previously requested assistance for this issue and are now following up on their request.
expected_outcome: The caller receives confirmation that the relevant team has been notified of their technical issue and is advised to monitor their email for updates on the resolution.
enquiry_text:
AY250529SQVSQ  Type: BGP 2.0. GRT. Claim Submission      Caller would like to request a follow up on their request for assistance on their inability to submit their claim. That when they click next it does not proceed.

AY250529MGT8C  Type: BGP 2.0, GRT Document Upload (Claims)     Caller mentioned after their last issue, they had tried going for another of their GRT submissions and make a claim for this. However, when caller tried uploading some documents, they get errors where it is indicated the document did not submit. Caller tried troubleshooting, similar to what they did with their other submission (clear cache) but the issue persists.
answer_text:
The relevant team(s) have been notified of the caller's situation with the BGP 2.0 GRT claim submission issue
The caller was advised to keep an eye on their email for any updates

claims.claim: The relevant team(s) have been notified of the caller's situation with the BGP 2.0 GRT claim submission issue
claims.source: Technical issues affecting the BGP portal are escalated to the relevant technology team for investigation. Users experiencing access issues or submission errors are advised to clear browser cache, use a supported browser (Chrome or Edge), and retry. Persistent issues are logged and resolved within 2 working days.

claims.claim: The caller was advised to keep an eye on their email for any updates
